name: Prize crossword No 26,184
preamble: A novel of the 4 21 across is based on six solutions not further defined in their clues.

clue.text: Damage home computer memory

blocks.note: to scratch something is to damage its surface
pad is slang for one's home or flat

explanation.surface: Someone frets that their home computer's memory has been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'home computer' as one phrase, but 'home' belongs with the wordplay and 'computer memory' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratchpad is a small fast area of storage a processor uses for temporary working data.

clue.text: Lots of wine on bench at market?

indicators.note: in a down entry one thing sitting on another is placed above it

blocks.note: a tun is a huge cask, holding lots of wine
a market stall is a trader's bench or table

explanation.surface: Crates of wine stacked on a trader's bench at a market.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the six theme answers with no definition in the clue, as the preamble says.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunstall is the northernmost of the six Staffordshire pottery towns federated into Stoke-on-Trent, called Turnhill by Bennett.

clue.text: River, one flowing out into dried grass

indicators.note: something flowing out leaves, so that letter departs from the word
going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: hay is grass cut and dried for fodder; it is split as HA...Y
the African river
I is the Roman numeral one, the letter that leaves

explanation.surface: A river empties out across a field of dried grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'one flowing out' look like a description of the river, but 'one' is a separate piece that departs from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanley is the commercial centre among the six Staffordshire pottery towns federated into Stoke-on-Trent, Bennett's Hanbridge.

clue.text: Cardinal's expression of disgust about Vatican City

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust
V is the international vehicle registration code for Vatican City

explanation.surface: A cardinal of the Church voices his disgust about goings-on in the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like the churchman, but it means a cardinal number; the 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers one, two, three and so on, of which five is one example.

clue.text: Philosophical reality that could excite sophist, say

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some philosophical notion of reality is the kind of thing that would get a sophist worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual 'for example' signal, but here its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: In metaphysics a hypostasis is the underlying substance or essential reality of a thing, as distinct from its attributes.

clue.text: Line on map in this other empire

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the following words, spanning their boundaries

blocks.note: runs across the ends and middle of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone traces a frontier on a map of a rival empire.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a border line, but the line is a climatic one on a weather map.
explanation.definitionFit: An isothere is a line on a chart joining places with the same mean summer temperature.

clue.text: At foot of tree trunk note fungi

indicators.note: in a down entry the foot is the bottom, so the first piece named is placed below the second

blocks.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A walker notices mushrooms growing at the base of a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' reads as a verb telling you to observe the fungi, but it supplies a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Boleti is the plural of boletus, a family of mushrooms with pores under the cap, including the cep.

clue.text: Church officer not operating in ecclesiastical office

indicators.note: not marks what follows as something to be taken away

blocks.note: a sexton looks after a church and its graveyard
a machine that is operating is on

explanation.surface: A church official is idle, not working in the parish office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' looks like a room, but in church usage an office is a service of set prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sext is one of the canonical hours of prayer, said around midday, the sixth hour of the day.

clue.text: Agency to make something happen when a country lass (no fool) enters London?

indicators.note: no means without, so something is taken away
to enter a place is to go inside it

blocks.note: the City is London's financial district; split as C...ITY
taken as written
the United States
taken as written
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A girl from the countryside arrives in London, and that sets something in motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country lass' reads as one phrase, but 'country' is a separate piece and the lass is left with only her first letter once the fool goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Causality is the relation of cause and effect, the agency by which one thing brings about another.

clue.text: Satisfactory note about money obtained from property on street

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or scattered, so the letters are rearranged
in an across entry, being on something means coming after it

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
OK means acceptable or satisfactory
taken as written, then rearranged
rent is income a landlord gets from property

explanation.surface: A landlord is satisfied with a note about the rent coming in from a property in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The city of Stoke-on-Trent was formed from the six Potteries towns, and is itself a theme entry with no definition. 'note' looks like a musical letter but is used whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoke-on-Trent is the Staffordshire city formed in 1910 by federating the six Potteries towns of Arnold Bennett's novels.

clue.text: Only half competent, you, not finishing, may offer excuse

indicators.note: keeping only half a word means dropping the other half
something not finishing stops short, so its end is lost

blocks.note: the first half of ABLE, meaning competent
you, the reader, are the SOLVERS; their end is cut off

explanation.surface: Someone who is only half competent and never finishes the job is full of excuses.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters often address the solver as 'you', so 'you' stands for SOLVERS, which loses its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to free them from blame or guilt, which is to excuse or pardon them.

clue.text: See 10
Cautious, making love without sex?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: charity is love in the Biblical sense, as in faith, hope and charity
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: Someone is wary about making love without actually having sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making love' reads as one phrase, but 'making' only links, and 'love' is the old Biblical sense of charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chary means being wary or reluctant to take risks, a close synonym of careful or cautious.

clue.text: Queen in bind in mad area associated with 4 21 across

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it; this applies at both levels

blocks.note: pots, from potty, meaning crazy; split as POT...S
to tie is to bind; split as T...IE
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A queen is in a mad predicament somewhere tied up with the theme.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a container within a container. 'mad' as POTS comes from potty, crazy. 4 21 across is FIVE TOWNS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potteries is the Staffordshire district of pottery manufacture made up of the towns of Bennett's Five Towns novels.

clue.text: Is wrongdoing admitted by newspapers being goody-goody?

indicators.note: something admitted is let in, so it goes inside

blocks.note: the press is newspapers collectively; split as PR...ESS
taken as written
sin is wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A question of whether the papers' confession of misconduct is just sanctimonious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the verb opening a question, but it is a piece taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Prissiness is fussy, prim propriety, the quality of being smugly well-behaved and easily shocked.

clue.text: Man under pressure to make contribution to phonetic dictionary

indicators.note: in a down entry being under something means coming below it

blocks.note: stress is pressure
Mark is a man's name

explanation.surface: A lexicographer is put under pressure to deliver his share of a pronunciation dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person doing the contributing, but it is just a forename.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronouncing dictionary uses symbols showing which syllable is emphasised, so those signs appear throughout it.

clue.text: Nice coppers to lie, almost fooling their senior officer

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes
fooling about suggests messing around, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the word minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Pleasant officers nearly get away with lying to their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city or simply pleasant; here its letters are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A police inspector ranks above constables and sergeants, so is a superior of the ordinary coppers.

clue.text: What may be converted to vitamin A, one trace dissolving

definitions.text: What may be converted to vitamin A

indicators.note: a thing dissolving breaks up and loses its form, so the letters re-form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: a substance turns into vitamin A, with just a trace left dissolving.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole first half, a description of what the substance does in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Carotene is the orange pigment in carrots, which the body breaks down to produce retinol.

clue.text: Kicked around a watery hole, maybe — must get dried

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes outside the other

blocks.note: to toe a ball is to kick it with the toe; split as TO...ED
a well is one example of a hole holding water

explanation.surface: Someone who has been splashing in a waterhole needs drying off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicked around' looks like a single phrasal verb, but 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To towel yourself is to rub yourself dry with a cloth, so towelled is a past form meaning wiped dry.

clue.text: Turns into barren areas of deserts, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters could be arranged another way

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Land gradually turns into the barren stretches typical of deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' looks like the shuffle signal but belongs to the definition; 'of' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To deforest land is to clear its trees, which often leaves it bare and infertile.

clue.text: Heartless criminal takes in holy books

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is removed
taking something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: a felon is a criminal
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted crook gets hold of some Bibles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' sounds like cruelty, but it removes the middle letter. Fenton is the sixth Potteries town, the one Bennett left out of his 'Five' Towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenton is one of the six towns federated in 1910 to form the city of Stoke-on-Trent in Staffordshire.

clue.text: More than one place has to be found after road junction

indicators.note: found after something means placed following it

blocks.note: a T-junction, where one road meets another at right angles
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Directions: more than one place lies past the next crossroads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' looks like part of 'has to be found', but supplies a verb of possession on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Towns are settlements, so the plural noun covers several places where people live.

clue.text: Someone feared two strike-breakers turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a rat is someone who works during a strike, and there are two of them

explanation.surface: A dreaded figure: a pair of scabs showing up for work.
explanation.walkthrough: A rat, like a scab, is a worker who refuses to join a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartar is a fierce, formidable or intractable person, someone others are wary of crossing.

clue.text: Fielder in the deep catches Kent's tail-ender

indicators.note: the one at the tail end is the last in line
to catch something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: long-on is a cricket fielding position near the boundary; split as LONG...ON
the final letter of the county name

explanation.surface: A cricket outfielder holds a catch to dismiss Kent's last batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a tail-ender is a weak batsman near the end of the order. Long-on is a deep fielding position. Longton is another of the Potteries towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Longton is one of the six Staffordshire towns making up Stoke-on-Trent, called Longshaw in Bennett's novels.

clue.text: Jam in cupboard, a third gone

indicators.note: losing a third means one of three equal parts is dropped

blocks.note: a locker is a small cupboard; its final third is lost

explanation.surface: A pot of jam in the cupboard, a third already eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' looks like the preserve, but it is a verb meaning to get stuck fast.
explanation.definitionFit: When a mechanism jams it seizes up and cannot move, which is what it does when it locks.

clue.text: Slumber is disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Burslem, the 'mother town' of the Potteries, is one of the six theme towns and appears as Bursley in Bennett's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Burslem is one of the six Staffordshire pottery towns federated into the city of Stoke-on-Trent.

clue.text: What may be furrowed, like soil mostly?

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: earth is usually this dark colour

explanation.surface: Something is furrowed as a ploughed field is.
explanation.walkthrough: Furrows suggest a field, but the furrowing here is wrinkling of the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: A brow is the forehead, which wrinkles into lines when someone frowns or worries.

clue.text: Size of paper hat

blocks.note: first meaning: a traditional British paper size, about 15 by 20 inches
second meaning: a monarch's headdress

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like asking how big a paper hat is; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old printing format of sheet and the ceremonial headwear a king or queen wears.

clue.text: Promoter of product making one's lager fantastic

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or bizarre, so the letters take a strange new form

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An advertising man makes a beer sound wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' looks like praise for the lager in an advert, which fits the definition, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloganeer coins catchy advertising phrases, so is someone who promotes goods for sale.
